title: Vacuum correlation measures as CFT partition functions
abstract: We show that in any $d$-dimensional CFT, the vacuum sandwiched Rényi mutual information (SRMI) of integer order $n$ between two disjoint balls maps to a CFT partition function on a manifold of topology $\#^{n-1}(S^1 \times S^{d-1})$, with moduli fixed by the ball configuration and single-ball modular flow. At $n=2$, it is given by the thermal partition function on $S^{d-1}$, upper-bounding the von Neumann mutual information. For $n>2$, SRMI diverges at finite separation due to a hot-spot limit of the partition function. Explicit CFT evaluations agree well with density matrix computations.

bite.hook: We map vacuum Rényi mutual information between disjoint balls to a CFT partition function on a complex manifold.
tldr: Studied vacuum sandwiched Rényi mutual information (SRMI) of integer order n between two disjoint balls in any d-dimensional CFT.
Mapped the SRMI mathematically to a conformal field theory partition function on a specific multi-sheeted manifold topology.
Found that at n=2 it equals a thermal partition function, while for n>2 it diverges at finite separation due to a hot-spot limit.
bite.whyItMatters: Connecting quantum information measures like Rényi mutual information to geometric partition functions gives physicists new mathematical tools to probe the structure of quantum field theories and spacetime.
bite.eli5: Imagine trying to measure how much two separate regions in a quantum sea share information. The author found a neat mathematical trick: instead of calculating the messy information directly, you can calculate the heat and energy flowing on a bizarre, multi-layered geometric donut.
